# Quick Description Table

*Page PDF 7*

## **Quick Description Table**
If you are looking for a brief description of the tavern, roll 1d10 and refer to the table below. If the tavern is a Silver Tier location, add 5 to the roll. If it is a Gold Tier location, add 10 to the roll. 

| 1d10 | Description |
|---|---|
| 1–3 | are filthy, the air mostly smoke, and where there are windows they are cracked and filthy. Puddles of ale, blood, or worse lie on the floor and the walls are full of rat holes. The furnishings are in terrible repair, besmirched and rotten. The venue is stiflingly hot and clammy in the summer, and ice cold in the winter. Genteel Poverty.  Whilst this tavern is clearly poor, it is lovingly looked after. Reeds on the floor are freshly laid |
| 4–5 | each Festag morning. The chamber pots and spitoons are cleaned every night, and possets of Tarrabeth are hung on the walls to dispel bad odours. A few cheap but tasteful religious icons and artworks adorn the walls. Conspicuous Piety.  It is difficult to tell if this is a tavern or a shrine with religious icons over the walls. Tracts of scripture are left on the tables, the strictures of gods and sayings of their priests are enscribed into the timbers of the |
| 6 | ceiling. In the Empire, most places of this sort appeal to Sigmarites, with hammers, comets, portraits of emperors past and present. Ulrican taverns may be decorated with axes, wolf pelts, and the heads of Orcs. Morrite venues place skulls in convenient alcoves and are decorated with bunches of raven feathers. Military or Naval Theme.  The owners of this venue are keen to come off as patriotic or adventurous, and decorate |
| 7 | the walls with military regalia and weaponry, or artefacts from sailing vessels and far off lands. The tavern has the feel of an antiques store with all the regalia and brick-a-brack on show, and it isn’t the most comfortable of venues, though among the trash are conversation pieces of geniune historical interest. Conspicuously Eccentric.  This tavern appeals to those with a taste for novelty. The walls are sturdy, but lean as precariously as a Tilean tower. Artwork with a scholarly or humourous theme adorns the walls, depicting scenes |
| 8 | from history or folklore. The furniture is a motley collection of mismatched pieces, much of which is second hand, and the walls of the venue are plastered in an eccentric paint scheme incorporating eye-catching patterns. Professional Pub.  A typical tavern of the Old World. The ground floor is of stone and the bar is roomy, with pine |
| 9–12 | furniture. The floors are wooden boards. Upper stories are half timber. Beer and wine is stored in a cool, mostly dry cellar. A few pieces of artwork or religious symbols decorate the walls. The mullion windows are protected from the weather by shutters. A roaring fire is lit in chilly weather, and candles or lanterns illuminate the rooms. |
| 13 | Conspicuously Eccentric.  As per result 8. |
| 14 | Military or Naval Theme.  As per result 7. Hunting Theme.  The tavern gives the impression of being a rural hunting lodge, even if it is in an inappropriate |
| 15 | location such as the middle of a city. The walls will be hung with antique crossbows and long rifles, nestled together with the trophy heads of various prized game animals, exotic beasts, and Orcs and Goblins. Pretentious Palace.  Money does not always buy good taste. The tavern is rather overdone in its attempts to impress, with decor that might not be out of place in a Bretonnian castle, foppish merchant residence, or Dwarf treasury. |
| 16 | Flagstones cover the floors, and most of the walls as well. Furnishings are outsized and garishly upholstered, and the rooms bedecked in extravagances such as tapestries, chandliers, and swathes of gold paint. Pandering to a Patron.  Someone has invested a lot of time and money into this place, and they are keen to let everyone who visits know about it. Whilst the tavern is well appointed, clean, and welcoming, it is rather upfront |
| 17 | in regard as to who its patron is. Their heraldry hangs from the walls as banners, shields, or tapestries, and may well be inscribed on tankards and beermats. Their portrait may be found on the walls of the bar, bedrooms, or even the privy. The patron will probably be a local aristocrat of note, but may be a guild or a coaching house. Splendid Venue.  The tavern has had a lot of money spent on making it a truely sumptuous place. The floors are covered in finely pointed flagstones swept morning and night. The furniture is finely crafted from oak and |
| 18–20 | hardwoods. The tankards are of fine pewter, embossed with the name and crest of the establishment. Windows are wrought from coloured patterned glass, and protected by shutters. Massive landscape paintings adorn the walls, depicting famous landmarks and scenes from history and legend. |
